title: Ken Tropin on Macro Hive Podcast- Markets, Risk, AI-Driven Technology, and What Comes Next

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Ken Tropin on Macro Hive Podcast- Markets, Risk, AI-Driven Technology, and What Comes Next.docx

summary:
Macro Hive (Dec 2025) with Graham founder Ken Tropin: conservative macro-focused philosophy (75% macro risk) vs pod shops, talent and AI, and 2026 views.
Main views: term premium is underpriced (US steepener), Japan/Europe/Canada hawkish, dollar range-bound, AI is real but expensive, stay small when conviction is low.

coverage.note: vs multistrats; AI and evolution; talent
culture; London/New York offices; 2025 trader performance
2026 Fed debate; term premium steepener; risk limits; AI bubble question
AI equities, Fed chair, tariffs and inflation, private credit
liquidity shock, fiscal stimulus, conviction rule, Japan hawkish
dollar range, US-China, geopolitics; Robin Hood philanthropy

completeness_estimate: 0.93 - first reader captured the views, risk rules and FX rule; missed the administration-pressure explanation of the stalled steepener and the outsider-Fed-chair uncertainty; one claim overstated economic weakness.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: the majority of our risk is in the macro markets which uh involves rate trading and uh FX trading and equity trading and um some commodity trading
claims.claim: Graham's book is about 75% macro risk: rates, FX, equities, some commodities, with much in fixed income relative value, curve (steepeners) and breakeven/inflation trades.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: keeping rest close to home is you know fortuitous and and and a good thing to do
claims.claim: Conservative philosophy: success across many cycles; sometimes constructive for views, other times keeping risk close to home is best; be innovative and opportunistic but careful.
claims.direction: reduce risk when conviction is low

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: in a multistract that might be 10% of the risk there or 15% of the risk with Graham it's 75 to 80% of the risk
claims.claim: Multi-strategy funds give only 10-15% of risk to macro; Graham offers 75-80% macro risk and custom-designed funds for clients.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: there's no way in our industry to rely on what you did, you know, say over the last two decades without trying to evolve in a constructive and thoughtful way
claims.claim: Quant approaches must evolve; computing power and AI are radically different, so firms must be at least competitive with the best thinking on AI and new quantitative opportunities.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: sometimes it's very uh it's a very virtuous thing to cultivate your own talent as opposed to sort of overpaying to get talent from a competitor
claims.claim: Talent strategy: grow young talent (Renaissance model hired mathematicians, not other hedge funds); build larger discretionary teams (about 25 PM teams, some with 15 people); slower but more controllable.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I truly believe in collaboration. I truly believe in helping others be successful. I believe really strongly in being airing on the side of being too patient
claims.claim: Culture of patience attracts PMs who would be cut quickly at multi-strategy pods.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: our traders have have uh done very well by being very tactical, opportunistic and not having really high levels of risk
claims.claim: In 2025 policy was fluid (tariffs, Supreme Court case), and Graham's traders did well being tactical with low risk levels.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: there are some people that believe that inflationary pressures will be very tough on the new Fed chair to uh cut rates
claims.claim: Debate on 2026: inflation constrains a new Fed chair versus slowdown allowing cuts; Tropin is skeptical of more cuts. Japan is raising rates and Europe sits in between.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I think term premium is underpriced. And so I like the steep nerve as a general statement. Obviously you got to know when to put it on and take it off
claims.claim: Highest-probability macro trade (Dec 2025): term premium is underpriced, so US curve steepeners; timing needed.
claims.indicator: US term premium; yield curve slope

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: our deficit is so extraordinarily large and so incurable from my perspective
claims.claim: US deficit size drives term premium: duration risk was ignored for years and the market will become more sensitive in the next year or two.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: most traders I know are you is using less of their risk limits than normal
claims.claim: Traders use less of their risk limits because policy or geopolitical shocks could be disruptive, which helps explain the curve going sideways after steepening earlier in 2025.

claims.speaker: Bilal Hafeez
claims.quote: People have made parallels to the dot period and and and people are using that as a template
claims.claim: AI equity correction analogies to the dot-com bust (credit event, Fed cutting) are used as a template for macro spillover.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I don't think this is some imaginary bubble or or meme event at all. I think AI is so for real it's kind of crazy and scary but having said that it's expensive
claims.claim: AI is a real, concentrated, expensive equity bet; a correction would be normal and warrants a risk-management watch on macro spillover.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: sometimes the market can get away from any central bank and we've seen that over and over again
claims.claim: Markets can run beyond central banks (Japan, Europe, Canada turning hawkish), though in the long run central banks regain control.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: you've got twothirds of the economy slowing outside of AI, right? So, that's slightly deflationary
claims.claim: US economy outside AI is slowing (deflationary), while tariffs act as a consumer tax companies pass on (car makers, EU goods at 15-20%), so inflation outcome is mixed.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: most people in private credit but not all uh are pretty good at understanding what you know risks they're taking
claims.claim: Private credit risk may be overblown because managers are sophisticated, but...

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: when there's a liquidity shock all bets are off right and um I you know we we saw that in private equity
claims.claim: ...a liquidity shock can force even well-run funds to suspend redemptions, so choose funds with strong risk management.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: there's going to be an enormous pressure on the new chair to to really stimulate the economy
claims.claim: Expect pressure for fiscal stimulus and Fed easing into 2026 midterms; bond markets were saying the opposite, which could reverse quickly, so be tactical.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: is when you don't have conviction, stay close to home
claims.claim: Rule: when there is no conviction, keep risk small; few aggressive traders survive, so run the book conservatively and accept bad cycles.
claims.direction: reduce risk when conviction is low

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: Japan is the most hawkish that I can remember
claims.claim: Japan is driving global rates higher (BoJ hawkish for the first time in decades), as are Canada and Europe, despite weak economies, a unprecedented pattern.

correction.issue: overstates: Tropin says the hawkishness comes even though Europe's economy is not strong, while the Asian economy may be pretty strong; he does not call all the economies weak
correction.fix: Japan is driving global rates higher (BoJ the most hawkish in decades), with Canada and Europe also turning hawkish even though Europe's economy is weak (Asia stronger), an unprecedented and hard-to-explain pattern.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: usually in forex uh you know the the country that has the most hawkish central bank has the strongest currency
claims.claim: FX rule: the most hawkish central bank has the strongest currency; when all are hawkish the dollar trades in a range (6 months), so take little risk either way.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: it's apparent that the US cannot decouple from China
claims.claim: US-China relationship is interdependent, not a Cold War paradigm, so escalation is limited (Taiwan tail risk remains); Russia/Ukraine resolution is naive to expect.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: every time I lose my humility, I I also usually lose money
claims.claim: Humility matters: loss of humility correlates with losses; heart-and-soul work effort drives success.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I showed up first. I left last.
claims.claim: Advice to young people: outwork others, positive attitude and can-do approach; AI's job effect unknowable. Graham is a $20bn, 250-person fund.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: people put on trades and then take them off. You've got a lot of pressure from the administration to get rates lower.
claims.claim: The US curve steepener stalled in late 2025 partly because of normal position churn and partly because the administration is pushing for lower rates, which leans against the term-premium repricing in the short run.
claims.indicator: US yield curve slope; political pressure on rates
claims.conditions: while the administration actively presses for lower rates
claims.testable: partly - relate curve moves to dated administration statements on rates

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: he's sort of an outsider not an insider. So, it'll be interesting to see how much uh you know um of of a sort of a team mentality there is at the Fed
claims.claim: Whether a Fed put protects equities in an AI correction is uncertain because the likely next chair (Hassett) is an outsider, so the committee's cohesion and reaction function are unknown.
claims.conditions: equity correction under a new outsider Fed chair
claims.testable: partly - track FOMC dissents and policy response to drawdowns under the new chair
